title: Sensex, Nifty Extend Losses for Fourth Day as Crude Oil Nears $100
excerpt: Brent crude surged past $98 a barrel on escalating US-Iran tensions and Houthi attacks on Red Sea tankers, dragging Indian benchmarks to their longest losing streak in seven weeks.
body:
• Sensex fell 363 points to 76,391 and Nifty dropped 126 points to 23,869 — their fourth consecutive session of losses, the longest in seven weeks
  • Brent crude jumped 4.52% to $98.32 per barrel after Houthis attacked Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea
  • Fifteen of 16 major sectors declined, with Oil & Gas, Pharma, and Realty among the hardest hit
  • Foreign institutional investors sold equities worth Rs 819 crore on Wednesday, adding to selling pressure

India's benchmark equity indices fell for a fourth consecutive session on Thursday as Brent crude surged past $98 a barrel, renewing concerns about inflation, a widening trade deficit, and compressed corporate margins.

The BSE Sensex declined 363.66 points, or 0.47%, to settle at 76,391.39 after dropping as much as 603 points during intraday trading to hit 76,151.98. The NSE Nifty 50 shed 126.65 points, or 0.53%, to close at 23,869.60. The four-day losing streak is the indices' longest in seven weeks, according to Reuters.

Crude Oil Surge Intensifies Market Pressure

Brent crude, the global benchmark, jumped 4.52% to $98.32 per barrel — its highest level in over five weeks — after Houthi forces claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian oil tankers transiting the Red Sea. The escalation marks the Houthis' most direct intervention in the wider US-Iran confrontation and has disrupted two of the world's most critical energy chokepoints: the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz.

West Texas Intermediate crude also surged more than 2% to $88.67 per barrel.

India, the world's third-largest crude oil importer and consumer, is acutely sensitive to rising energy costs. Higher oil prices threaten to stoke domestic inflation, widen the trade gap, and squeeze profit margins across sectors.

"With crude oil prices approaching the $100-per-barrel mark amid concerns over further disruptions to global energy supplies, investor sentiment remained subdued as markets reassessed inflation risks and corporate margins."

— Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited

Broad-Based Selloff Across Sectors

Fifteen of the 16 major NSE sectors ended lower. The Nifty Oil & Gas index was the worst performer, declining nearly 1%, followed by Pharma, Realty, PSU Banks, and Cement. The broader market fared no better — the Nifty Smallcap 100 and Midcap 100 indices both dropped around 1%.

Only FMCG and MidSmall IT & Telecom traded in the green.

Among Sensex stocks, Adani Ports, Bajaj Finance, InterGlobe Aviation, Axis Bank, State Bank of India, and Tata Steel were the biggest drags. Drugmaker Dr Reddy's Laboratories fell 1.4% and Cipla dropped 1.6% after reporting weak quarterly results. Oil marketing company HPCL slid 2.5%.

On the positive side, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Consultancy Services, and Bajaj Finserv were among the few gainers. SpiceJet surged 10% after a Reuters report said Adani Group may launch an airline, fueling acquisition speculation.

Private lender IndusInd Bank dropped 6% despite a jump in June-quarter profit on lower provisions, as investors booked profits after the stock had rallied 7.2% in six sessions ahead of results.

Geopolitical Risk Dominates Sentiment

"The key question for markets is whether the recent escalation represents a temporary bout of geopolitical posturing or the start of a more prolonged conflict between U.S. and Iran. A sustained rise above $100 per barrel would pose a meaningful risk to growth, inflation and market performance."

— Mitesh Jain, Head of Broking, Sanctum Wealth

Foreign Institutional Investors added to the pressure, offloading Indian equities worth Rs 819.20 crore on Wednesday after a one-day pause, according to exchange data. The selloff comes during an otherwise steady earnings season, but analysts say geopolitical risk has overtaken fundamentals as the dominant market driver.

Global Markets Mixed

Asian markets presented a mixed picture on Thursday. South Korea's KOSPI rallied 4.4%, while Japan's Nikkei 225, Shanghai's SSE Composite, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng also posted gains. Taiwan's weighted index declined about 1%, and Singapore's Straits Times slipped 0.8%.

In the US, the S&P 500 fell 0.14% and the Nasdaq declined 0.57% on Wednesday. European markets were also trading lower on Thursday.

What to Watch

Markets will closely watch Infosys and IndiGo quarterly results due later Thursday. More broadly, the trajectory of crude oil prices and any developments in the US-Iran standoff will dictate near-term direction. Some analysts see the pullback as an entry opportunity to gradually accumulate high-quality stocks in growth segments at attractive valuations.
